report.headline: Feeling wrung out by sticky heat?
report.quick_read: Heat and humidity in the Desert Southwest may be part of what some people notice today, including feeling more tired, sleep running warm, or effort feeling harder. Space weather is low. Earth sensors picked up natural atmospheric tones and a quiet ground pattern.

regional_watch.selection_method: At least two fixed anchors must support the same driver.
regional_watch.copy:
• Desert Southwest US: Heat and humidity are the key driver today, supported by Phoenix and Las Vegas. Some people may notice more fatigue or sleep disruption, and effort may feel harder.
• Elsewhere in the U.S.: No other standout regional patterns rose to today’s watch level.

space_watch.copy: Space weather is low today. The day’s geomagnetic peak is Kp 1.3, which is also where it sits now. The solar wind is near 256 km/s, and the magnetic field is oriented northward at the moment—conditions that go with a calm day. No Earth‑directed solar eruptions are indicated; a catalog count alone doesn’t imply impact.

earth_signal.health_language: Possible effects may use 'may', 'can', or 'some people notice' without an appended disclaimer.
earth_signal.copy: Natural atmospheric tones were detected today, with measured frequencies near 7.49 Hz, 14.56 Hz, 22.17 Hz, 29.07 Hz, and 35.92 Hz. Ground magnetic sensors indicated a quiet pattern spread across the measured frequencies. Measurements came from stations including BOU and CMO.

major_events.selection_method: Fresh yellow-or-higher GDACS/USGS events, deduplicated and capped.

platform_copy.facebook:
Feeling wrung out by sticky heat? In parts of the Desert Southwest, today’s warmth and moisture may be part of what some people notice—feeling more tired than usual, sleep running warm, or everyday effort feeling harder.

Regional Watch
• Desert Southwest US: Heat and humidity are the main story, supported by Phoenix and Las Vegas today. Some people may notice fatigue or sleep disruption, and physical effort can feel tougher.

Space Watch
Space weather is low today, which points to a calm background in near‑Earth space. Think of this as the space environment staying quiet. The day’s peak measure of magnetic unsettledness (the K‑index) reached 1.3, and that’s also where it sits now. The solar wind is moving around 256 km/s at the moment, and the interplanetary magnetic field is pointed north, both consistent with a quiet day. A catalog count alone doesn’t mean an impact, and no Earth‑directed events are indicated.

Earth Signal
Natural atmospheric tones that scientists track were detectable today. After those tones are identified, the specific frequencies can be listed; they included about 7.49 Hz, 14.56 Hz, 22.17 Hz, 29.07 Hz, and 35.92 Hz. Ground magnetic sensors showed a quiet, even pattern across the measured range, without notable spikes.

What this means for you
If you’re in Phoenix or Las Vegas, heat and humidity may be part of what you notice in your body today. Elsewhere across the U.S., no other standout regional patterns rose to today’s watch level.

Full report: gaiaeyes.com
Personalized patterns: gaiaeyes.com/app

If you’re in Phoenix or Las Vegas, this is where it’s strongest right now. Full daily report: gaiaeyes.com

In the Desert Southwest, warm and humid air may be part of what some people notice—more fatigue, sleep running warm, or everyday effort feeling tougher. Strongest impacts are around Phoenix and Las Vegas today.
